svg.desc: A05, VOYAGER CILIA ARRAY. Original project: Artificial Cilia Creation for Advanced Sensor Devices. Session A: Math, Physics & Chemistry. Scientific question: Can actuation-aware inversion separate fluid velocity from viscosity more accurately than passive cilia deflection alone? Testable hypothesis: Measurements at several drive frequencies and orientations will improve parameter identifiability, provided actuator torque and cilium stiffness are independently calibrated.. svg.text: Artificial Cilia Creation for Advanced Sensor Devices
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Proposed mission: create an active flow-sensing skin whose compliant cilia
both probe their fluid environment and report deflection. Evaluate whether
controlled actuation improves sensitivity to velocity and viscosity while
maintaining robustness to temperature, fouling, and structural variation.
The mission analogy is a compact sensor surface for fluid-handling
instruments and environmental probes, with qualification treated as future
Can actuation-aware inversion separate fluid velocity from viscosity more
accurately than passive cilia deflection alone?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT

Low Reynolds number and small deflection justify the first model only over a
Large bending, wall effects, magnetic interactions, and viscoelastic fluid
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
A sensor-integrated magnetic cilium precedent does not demonstrate space
readiness. Viscosity–velocity degeneracy, fabrication scatter, and
wall-dependent flow can limit generalization between channels.
